gaps.sentence: He ___ spend so much time on his phone; it is affecting his sleep.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't' advises against an action: shouldn't spend.

gaps.sentence: ___ I borrow your charger for a minute?
gaps.explanation: 'May' is the polite way to ask permission: May I borrow.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ to buy the textbook; copies are available in the library.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' plus the infinitive expresses absence of obligation: don't have to buy.

gaps.sentence: Applications ___ be submitted in person, not by post.
Where is Anna? I am not sure — she ___ be in the library.
gaps.hint: an uncertain possibility, not really sure
gaps.explanation: 'Might' expresses a possibility the speaker is unsure about: might be.

gaps.sentence: If I were you, I ___ take the earlier train.
gaps.hint: if I were you plus would
gaps.explanation: 'If I were you' is followed by 'would': would take.

gaps.sentence: There was plenty of food left, so the guests ___ have been hungry.
gaps.explanation: The evidence (leftover food) rules out hunger: can't have been.

gaps.sentence: I ___ have known you were in hospital — nobody told me.
gaps.explanation: 'Couldn't have' means it was impossible to do: couldn't have known.
